blocks.text: **Data Interpretation (DI)** tests the ability to read and analyse data presented in **tables, bar/line graphs, pie charts and caselets**, then compute values, ratios, percentages and trends — a core, high-weight CSAT skill.

rows: Data embedded in a paragraph — extract into a table.

items: **Read the title, axes, units and legend** before the questions.
For pie charts, **1% = 3.6°** of the circle.
Use **approximation** and percentage shortcuts to save time.
Watch **units** (lakh vs crore, % vs absolute).
**Formats**: tables, bar/line/pie charts, mixed/caselet; read the **title, units, legend** first.
**Pie chart**: each sector = (value/total)×360°; convert % ↔ degrees (1% = 3.6°).
**% change, ratios, averages, growth** across categories are the common asks; approximate to save time.
**Traps**: absolute vs percentage, cumulative vs individual, different bases; watch units (₹ crore vs lakh).

blocks.text: Solved: In a pie chart, a sector of 90° = **25%** of the total. || If sales grew from 200 to 250, growth = 50/200×100 = **25%**. || Average of 4 items summing to 1200 = **300**.

prelimsPointers: Read **axes, units, legend and footnotes** first.
Use **percentage & ratio shortcuts**; approximate where options are far apart.

glossary.definition: Analysing data given in tables or graphs to answer quantitative questions.
A circular chart showing parts of a whole, where 1% equals 3.6 degrees.

blocks.text: **Data-sufficiency** questions ask not for the answer but whether the **given statements provide enough information** to answer. The skill is judging sufficiency **without fully solving**.

rows: Statement I alone is sufficient, II alone is not.
Statement II alone is sufficient, I alone is not.
Both together are sufficient, neither alone.

items: **Evaluate each statement independently** first.
Decide sufficiency **without computing the final value**.
Only if neither alone suffices, **combine** them.
A statement is sufficient if it yields a **unique** answer.
You judge **whether the given statements are ENOUGH** to answer — NOT the actual value.
Standard options: (a) Statement I alone sufficient, (b) II alone, (c) both together, (d) either alone, (e) neither.
**Method**: test each statement **independently**, then together; don't do unnecessary calculation; beware assuming extra info.
A statement that gives a **unique** answer is sufficient; multiple possible answers = insufficient.

blocks.text: Solved: 'What is x?' I: x is even; II: x is prime. Alone each insufficient; together x is an even prime → **x=2** → both together sufficient (option c).

prelimsPointers: Test **Statement I alone**, then **II alone**, then **both together**.
A statement is sufficient only if it gives a **unique** answer.
Don't carry assumptions from one statement into the other when testing 'alone'.
Combine statements **only if** neither is individually sufficient.
Avoid unnecessary full calculation — save time.
Data sufficiency = decide if statements **suffice**, don't compute the value.
Test **each statement alone first**, then together.
A statement is sufficient only if it yields a **unique** answer.
Don't assume information beyond what's stated.

glossary.definition: A question type asking whether the given statements are enough to answer, not the answer itself.
A single definite value/outcome, the test of a statement's sufficiency.

blocks.text: **Probability** measures the likelihood of an event, ranging from **0 (impossible) to 1 (certain)**. It is computed as favourable outcomes over total outcomes, with rules for combined events.

items: Coin: 2 outcomes; die: 6; **deck of cards: 52** (4 suits, 13 each, 26 red/26 black).
**P(certain)=1, P(impossible)=0**; probabilities sum to 1.
**Probability** P(E) = (favourable outcomes)/(total outcomes); **0 ≤ P ≤ 1**; P(certain)=1, P(impossible)=0.
**Complement**: P(not E) = 1 − P(E).
**Addition**: P(A∪B) = P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B); mutually exclusive → P(A∩B)=0.
**Multiplication (independent)**: P(A∩B) = P(A)·P(B).
Sample spaces: **die = 6, coin = 2, deck = 52 (26 red/black, 4 suits of 13, 12 face cards, 4 aces)**.

blocks.text: Solved: P(even on a die) = 3/6 = **½**. || P(a king from a deck) = 4/52 = **1/13**. || Two coins: P(both heads) = ½·½ = **¼**. || P(at least one head in 2 tosses) = 1 − ¼ = **¾**.

prelimsPointers: A **deck has 52 cards** (26 red, 26 black; 4 suits; 12 face cards).
Sum of probabilities of all outcomes = **1**.
Deck of 52: **4 aces, 12 face cards, 13 per suit, 26 red/black**.

glossary.definition: A measure (0 to 1) of the likelihood of an event occurring.
Events that cannot occur together, so P(A∩B)=0.
Events where one's occurrence does not affect the other's, so P(A∩B)=P(A)·P(B).
